om.heroTitle: Danceitude was built because the dance community deserves better tools

intro.p1: Danceitude started with a problem I knew all too well myself.
intro.p2: As a dancer at Evolution Danseklubb in Sarpsborg, I experienced how clunky booking private lessons could be. Open time slots were shared in a Google Docs document. Dancers and parents had to find an open slot, write themselves in, and keep track of the booking themselves.
intro.p3: It worked. But it could work so much better.
intro.p4: I hold a master's degree specializing in interaction design, and work as a Digital Marketing Manager and designer at SkyeTec, as well as an Interaction Specialist at MyTalent. I'm passionate about building digital solutions grounded in the people who will actually use them.
intro.p5: So I didn't just want to build another booking tool. I wanted to find out what dancers, parents and trainers actually need.

developedTogether.heading: Developed together with the dance community
developedTogether.p1: Danceitude started as part of my master's thesis and was developed through a user-centered design process.
developedTogether.p2: Through workshops with dancers, parents and trainers, we mapped out the challenges with the current way of doing things. Participants shared their experiences, discussed their needs, and sketched out how they wanted a better solution to work.
developedTogether.p3: The ideas were then developed into prototypes, tested with real users, and refined based on the feedback we got.
developedTogether.conclusion: Danceitude isn't built on assumptions about what the dance community needs. It's built together with the people who know the everyday reality best.

threeRoles.heading: One app. Three roles. A simpler dance routine.
threeRoles.subheading: Danceitude brings booking, training, development and competitions together in one place. Every user gets the features and overview suited to their role.

moreThanBooking.heading: More than a booking app
moreThanBooking.p1: Danceitude started with a need for an easier way to book private lessons.
moreThanBooking.p2: But through the work with dancers, parents and trainers, it became clear the need was bigger. A dancer's routine consists of training, goals, levels, competitions, results and development over time. Today, much of this information is scattered across documents, messages, notes and different systems.
moreThanBooking.p3: Danceitude brings it all together in one place. The goal is to make it easier to organize the dance routine, track progress over time, and create better collaboration between dancers, parents and trainers.

beginning.heading: This is just the beginning
beginning.p1: Danceitude will keep being developed together with the dance community.
beginning.p2: Feedback from dancers, parents and trainers will continue to be an important part of how the app improves and which features get built next.
beginning.quote: The best solutions aren't built for the users. They're built together with them.

footerCard.tagline: Developed together with the dance community. Built for the whole dance routine.

support.heading: Support
support.subheading: Need help with Danceitude? Here are answers to common questions.

faq.q: How do I book a private lesson?
faq.a: Go to "Book lesson" from the dashboard, choose a trainer, date and time, and confirm the booking.

faq.q: How do I cancel a lesson?
faq.a: Go to "My lessons" and tap the lesson you want to cancel. You'll find the cancel button there.

faq.q: I forgot my password – what do I do?
faq.a: Go to the login page and tap "Forgot your password?". You'll receive an email with a link to reset it.

faq.q: How do I delete my account?
faq.a: Go to the Profile page and scroll to the bottom. You'll find the "Delete account" button there. Account deletion is permanent and can't be undone.

faq.q: I'm a trainer – how do I post open times?
faq.a: Go to "Add availability" in the menu, choose a date and the times you're available, and tap "Post times".
